case_name: Abbayolla M. Subba Reddy vs Padmamma
facts_of_case: The respondent-wife filed a suit for maintenance from the petitioner-husband, claiming Rs.1,000/- per month and Rs.13,000/- towards the cost of gold chain and other ornaments gifted to her by her father.

legal_principles.principle: The Legislature intended to confer statutory right for maintenance and alimony even in cases where her marriage contravenes the conditions prescribed under Section 5 and is declared to be null and void under Section 11 of that Act.
legal_principles.held: It has to be inferred that the Legislature intended to confer statutory right for maintenance and alimony even in cases where her marriage contravenes the conditions prescribed under Section 5 and is declared to be null and void under Section 11 of that Act.

legal_principles.principle: The Parliament codified the personal law relating to Hindus and enacted the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, The Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956, The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 and the The Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
legal_principles.held: In view of the divergent schools governing the personal laws of the Hindus, the Parliament codified the personal law relating to the Hindus and enacted the said four Acts.

outcome.final_order: The court held that a Hindu woman who is married after the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 comes into force cannot maintain a claim for maintenance under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956.

keywords: C. Obuta Konda Reddy v. Pedda Venkala Lakshmamma
